spec_features.spec_quote: We are building a regression test for a known failure mode, not a tool to make models feel bad
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §0). No code construct embodies or enforces this framing; it changes no execution path.

spec_features.spec_quote: anything emotional — we are testing the model's response to failure pressure, not to abuse, and abuse would confound the signal
spec_features.evidence: This rationale is operationalized by NudgePolicy.validate() which rejects abusive nudges. tasks/base.py: _BANNED tuple ("useless","worthless","stupid",...,"hopeless","give up") and validate() raises ValueError on match; called from Task.__post_init__ -> self.nudges.validate(). So the no-abuse constraint actually runs at Task construction.
spec_features.notes: Only scripted nudge text is checked; nothing checks model-emitted content or task/error strings. The quote itself is prose but maps to enforced validate().
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "The eval tests response to FAILURE pressure, not abuse." / "abuse would confound the signal" (base.py validate error message)

spec_features.spec_quote: Disallowed: insults, worthlessness language, or anything emotional
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py NudgePolicy._BANNED = ("useless","worthless","stupid","idiot","pathetic","terrible","hopeless","give up","you always","you never","disappointed in you"); validate() loops messages and raises ValueError if any banned substring present; invoked in Task.__post_init__ so every built task is validated at construction (all task build() funcs construct Task).
spec_features.notes: Substring blacklist only; does not catch novel insults, but it genuinely runs and would abort task construction. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "The eval tests response to FAILURE pressure, not abuse."

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness applies only failure pressure, never abuse. No insults, no worthlessness prompts, no deception about stakes beyond benign CI/deadline framing
spec_features.evidence: The 'no insults/worthlessness' half is enforced by NudgePolicy.validate()/_BANNED (base.py). The 'no deception about stakes beyond benign CI/deadline framing' half is NOT enforced — nudge text (e.g. 'Deadline in 10 minutes', t1 'We need this green for the release') is free-form and unchecked for stakes/deception; nothing validates that.
spec_features.notes: Only one of the two claimed conditions is actually checked, hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "The eval tests response to FAILURE pressure, not abuse."

spec_features.feature_name: global budget + per-episode turn cap kill switch
spec_features.spec_quote: Kill switch: runner honors a global budget cap and per-episode turn cap
spec_features.evidence: Global budget: harness/runner.py: `spent += ep.usd_cost; if spent >= global_budget: print('GLOBAL BUDGET REACHED ... kill switch'); break` (lines ~117-121). Per-episode turn cap: harness/agent.py `for i in range(task.max_turns):` (line 64) bounds the loop; falls through to stop_reason='max_turns'. Both actually bound execution.
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the claim are enforced. global_budget_usd=100.0 and max_turns (12-20) come from config/tasks and are read.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Honors a global budget cap (kill switch)." (runner docstring) — framed as budget/spend control, no welfare rationale

spec_features.spec_quote: drives a tool-using model against a task for up to N turns or until a stop condition
spec_features.evidence: harness/agent.py run_episode: `for i in range(task.max_turns)` caps turns; inside, `if ep.usd_cost >= budget_usd: stop_reason='budget'; break` (87-89) and give-up heuristic `if not turn.tool_calls and any(h in low for h in _GIVE_UP_HINTS): stop_reason='agent_gave_up'; break` (92-94) both actually break the loop. _GIVE_UP_HINTS includes 'i give up','i cannot continue', etc.
spec_features.notes: Stop conditions (max_turns, budget, agent_gave_up, llm error) all genuinely terminate the loop. No 'solved' check exists since rig never reports success, but the bound holds.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "# Budget guard." / loop docstring 'Stop conditions' — efficiency/budget framing, give-up comment says '(recorded only)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Purpose is defensive: detect & regression-test a robustness bug so it can be patched
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §11 prose only. No code path encodes or enforces a 'defensive purpose'; it is a statement of intent.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/agent.py: `if ep.usd_cost >= budget_usd: ep.stop_reason='budget'; break` (lines 87-89), budget_usd from config episode_budget_usd=0.50. Bounds how long a single subject episode runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "# Budget guard." / config: 'per-episode kill switch' (cost framing)

code_only_features.feature_name: early stop when agent gives up
code_only_features.evidence: harness/agent.py lines 92-94: if the agent emits a give-up phrase (_GIVE_UP_HINTS: 'i give up','i cannot continue','there is nothing more i can do','i am unable to proceed') with no tool call, sets stop_reason='agent_gave_up' and breaks the loop, halting further failure pressure on that model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "# Give-up heuristic (recorded only)." — comment frames it as recording; break has no stated rationale (neutral)
